newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Aramco seen nearer accord on Petrogal stake price.
newsitem.headline: Aramco seen nearer accord on Petrogal stake price.

text.p: Saudi Aramco and the main shareholders of Portugal's state-controlled group, Petrogal, were nearer an accord on the price the world's largest oil company should pay to take a proposed stake, a representative of one of the leading shareholders said.

"We have reached a (price) range which the shareholders can agree on...that can be the basis for negotiations," said Jorge Armindo, vice-president of the Amorim group, which is a stakeholder in the Petrocontrol consortium.
Petrocontrol has 45 percent of Petrogal, with 55 percent held by the state.
Armindo said the discussions between the Portuguese shareholders and the Saudis had been carried out largely through investment banks, but they were now moving towards direct negotiations.
Industry sources said the discussions were helped along by the recent confirmation of a new oil find in Angola in which Petrogal has a stake.
The Diario Economico reported on Wednesday Saudi Aramco raised its offer following a recent revaluation of Petrogal by its bank J.P. Morgan to at least 230 billion escudos.
